# Checking Locus Sizes and Variant Counts

The purpose of this script is to check the sizes of loci and count the number of
variants in them. The goal is to pay special attention to the long loci and 
identify a threshold at which we might be able to prune based on significance.

### 1) Load in Libraries and Set Input Locations

```{r} 
#Call needed libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(pbapply)

#Set input directory
inp_dir <- "C:/Users/mconery/Box/Mitchell_Work_Files/Meta-Analysis_Fine-Mapping/Data/Defining_Loci/"
#Set input files
ALL_file <- paste0(inp_dir, "sig_loci.ALL.plus_var_counts.csv")
AFR_file <- paste0(inp_dir, "sig_loci.AFR.plus_var_counts.csv")
AMR_file <- paste0(inp_dir, "sig_loci.AMR.plus_var_counts.csv")
EAS_file <- paste0(inp_dir, "sig_loci.EAS.plus_var_counts.csv")
EUR_file <- paste0(inp_dir, "sig_loci.EUR.plus_var_counts.csv")
```

### 2) Read in Files and Make a Basic Histogram of Locus sizes by bp

The goal here is simply to understand the distribution of sizes, so we can use 
the information to begin scoping out our work. 

```{r}

#Read in files
ALL_raw <- read.table(ALL_file, sep = ",", header = TRUE)
AFR_raw <- read.table(AFR_file, sep = ",", header = TRUE)
AMR_raw <- read.table(AMR_file, sep = ",", header = TRUE)
EAS_raw <- read.table(EAS_file, sep = ",", header = TRUE)
EUR_raw <- read.table(EUR_file, sep = ",", header = TRUE)

make_size_plot <- function(sig_raw){
  # Calculate scaling factor and percentiles
  max_length <- max(sig_raw$LENGTH)
  max_pv <- max(sig_raw$PV_1e.00)
  scale_factor <- max_length / max_pv
  percentiles <- quantile(sig_raw$LENGTH, c(0.95, 0.99))  # Calculate percentiles
  
  # Create dual-axis cumulative distribution plot
  p<-ggplot(sig_raw) +
    stat_ecdf(aes(x = LENGTH), geom = "step", color = "blue", size = 1.2) +
    stat_ecdf(aes(x = PV_1e.00 * scale_factor), geom = "step", color = "red", size = 1.2) +
    geom_vline(
      xintercept = percentiles,
      linetype = "dashed",
      color = "darkgray",
      linewidth = 0.8
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      name = "Locus Length",
      limits = c(0, 6e6),
      sec.axis = sec_axis(~./scale_factor, name = "Number of Variants")
    ) +
    ylab("Cumulative Proportion") +
    theme(
      panel.background = element_blank(),
      axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.text.x.bottom = element_text(color = "blue"),
      axis.title.x.bottom = element_text(color = "blue"),
      axis.text.x.top = element_text(color = "red"),
      axis.title.x.top = element_text(color = "red"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12)
    ) +
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = percentiles+1.8e5,
      y = 1.02,
      label = c("95th", "99th"),
      color = "darkgray",
      size = 4,
      vjust = 0
    )
  print(p)
}

#Make ALL plot
make_size_plot(ALL_raw)

```

I note that there is a single variant in the locus QTL_UA.chr1:145250001-146000000. This is not a mistake. There is one variant with a p-value of 10^-94.

### 3) Make histograms for ancestral populations

```{r}
make_size_plot(AFR_raw)
```

```{r}
make_size_plot(AMR_raw)
```

```{r}
make_size_plot(EAS_raw)
```

```{r}
make_size_plot(EUR_raw)
```
